title: Paired scan execution
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $y$ be a bit string, let $B$ be a natural-number register bound, and let $I$ be a simulator state with two Boolean flags $f_0,f_1$. Suppose $u,u'$ are bit strings of equal length, the register valuation $v$ has every register at most $B$, and its registers $E,Q_3,Q_4$ satisfy $v(E)=v(Q_3)+2|u|$ and $v(Q_4)+2|u|le B$. Suppose also that, for every $i<|u|$, the input bits at positions $v(Q_3)+2i$ and $v(Q_4)+2i$ in $y$ (taken to be false when out of range) equal the $i$th bits of $u$ and $u'$, respectively (also taken false when out of range). Then the coded simulator has a finite execution from the paired scan-test state, with valuation $v$, to the paired scan-finish state whose simulator state is obtained by folding the paired transition rule for $I$ over the zipped lists $u,u'$, and whose valuation agrees with $v$ except that registers $Q_3,Q_4$ are advanced to $v(Q_3)+2|u|$ and $v(Q_4)+2|u|$. Throughout the execution, the simulator's guard conditions hold and all registers remain at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite nondeterministic Turing machine N over Boolean symbols
Simulator state I and Boolean flags f₀,f₁
Bit strings u,u′ have equal length
Initial register valuation v is bounded by B
For each i < |u|, the designated y bit equals the i-th bit of u, with out-of-range bits false
For each i < |u|, the other designated y bit equals the i-th bit of u′, with out-of-range bits false
